text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I draft, there's one thing you need to decide and a few questions.

**The "same cleaner every single time" promise.** What you've told me supports a regular cleaner plus a named backup. It doesn't support "every single time." Cleaners get sick, take vacations and leave. Seven of your 18 left last year. These customers left partly because their cleaner changed, so if the promise breaks once it confirms the reason they left, and this time you put it in writing. Something your facts do support: *"You'll have one regular cleaner. If they're ever out, it's your named backup, someone you'll already know, never a stranger."* Which version do you want? If you'll commit to more, like telling them ahead of time whenever the backup is coming, tell me and I'll include it.

**Questions (the most useful first):**

1. **Has anything changed to keep cleaners from leaving?** For example a raise, benefits, or better retention this year. A backup system answers "a different person keeps showing up." It doesn't answer "your staff keeps quitting." Anything you've done about that is the strongest thing this email can say.
2. **What exactly is the $99 offer?** Is it the first cleaning only, then $165 every other week? Is there a deadline or a minimum commitment? Customers who left over price will look for the catch.
3. **What do customers get for the extra $25?** You have employees and insurance on every visit. Do you also have a re-clean guarantee, background checks, or supplies included? Do you know for sure the app services use uninsured contractors? I won't claim that unless you can confirm it.
4. **Who signs it, and how do they rebook?** Your name, the company name, and a link or phone number.
5. **Is anything coming that they'll find out about anyway?** For example a price increase, or a change to the service area. It's better to mention it now than have them find out after they come back.

Go with your version. I can't promise every single time because of sick days and holidays, but I want it as strong as it can be without being false. I can commit to a regular cleaner and a named backup for every customer. I haven't decided on telling them ahead of time when the backup's coming, so leave that out.

1. We started giving each customer a regular cleaner in July. Since then 1 of our 18 cleaners has left. I don't have anything else to add on raises or benefits.
2. $99 is the first cleaning only, then the regular $165 every other week. The offer ends December 31. There's no contract, and they can cancel any time.
3. Yes, the app services here mostly use contractors who carry no insurance on the visit. I don't know about a re-clean guarantee, background checks, or supplies, so leave those out.
4. Lisa Grant, owner, Brightway Home Cleaning. They can rebook by replying to the email or calling 555-0164.
5. Nothing that I know of.

I've written the email around your regular-cleaner-plus-backup commitment. Body and sign-off come to about 165 words.

<final_document>
Subject: One regular cleaner, and $99 to come back

Hi,

When customers left us last year, they gave two main reasons: price, and a different cleaner showing up each time. The second was our fault. Seven of our 18 cleaners left, and about 4 in 10 customers had their cleaner change.

In July we fixed that. Every customer now has one regular cleaner and a named backup for sick days and holidays. Whoever comes to your door will be one of two people you know by name. Since July, 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.

On price: an every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom home costs $165 with us and about $140 with the app services. The extra pays for cleaners who are our employees, paid $21 an hour, with insurance on every visit. Most app cleaners here are contractors with no insurance on the visit.

Come back and your first cleaning is $99, then $165. There's no contract and you can cancel any time. The offer ends December 31.

Just reply to this email or call 555-0164.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

- **Turnover:** The email admits last year's turnover before the fix. Without that, "since July, 1 has left" doesn't mean much, and these customers already know they lost their cleaner.
- **The backup:** I didn't say customers will have met their backup, because you didn't tell me they do. If they do meet them, "someone you've already met" would be stronger.
- **Offer deadline:** "The offer ends December 31" doesn't say whether that's the last day to book or the last day for the cleaning itself. If you mean one of those, say which.
